seoDescription: Master ERPNext workflows by learning how to configure a multi-stage approval process from scratch. This guide walks you through creating a custom purchase order workflow, defining workflow states like 'draft', 'waiting for review', and 'approved', and setting up transition rules with specific user actions. Understand the core concepts of states and actions, assign role-based permissions for editing and approvals (e.g., Purchase User, Purchase Manager), and see the workflow in action from initial request to final submission.

chapters.description: This chapter shows how to start building a new workflow, name it, and link it to a specific document type like a Purchase Order.

chapters.description: Plan the multi-step approval process by mapping out the roles, actions, and document states involved in a purchase order review.

chapters.title: Configuring Workflow States and Permissions
chapters.description: Create the required document states within ERPNext and assign specific user roles that are allowed to edit the document at each stage.

chapters.title: Defining Workflow Transition Rules
chapters.description: This section details how to create the transition rules that connect each workflow state with a specific user action and the associated role permissions.

chapters.title: Activating and Demonstrating the Workflow
chapters.description: See how to save, activate, and then test the complete purchase order workflow in a live demonstration from creation to final submission.

summary:
## Core Workflow Concepts
- **Workflow State**: Represents the current stage of a document in the approval process (e.g., `Draft`, `Waiting for Review`, `Approved`).
- **Workflow Action**: The specific action a user takes to move the document from one state to the next (e.g., `Submit for Review`, `Approve`).

## Workflow Creation Process
1.  **Design the Logic**: Map out the sequence of states, actions, and user roles involved in your process.
2.  **Create the Workflow**: In ERPNext, create a new workflow and link it to a specific document type (e.g., `Purchase Order`).
3.  **Define States**: In the `States` table, list all possible states the document can be in and define which user role is allowed to edit the document at each state.
4.  **Define Transition Rules**: In the `Transition Rules` table, connect the states by defining the required user **action** and the **allowed role** to move from a starting state to the next state.
5.  **Activate**: Save and enable the workflow to make it active for all new documents of that type.

## Example: 3-Stage Purchase Order Approval
This video demonstrates a workflow with three key roles:
- **Requester** (`Purchase User`): Creates the draft and submits it for review.
- **Checker** (`Purchase Manager`): Reviews the submission.
- **Approver** (`Head of Department`): Gives the final approval.

### Approval Flow:
- **State**: `Draft`
  - **Action**: `Submit for Review` (by `Purchase User`)
  - **Next State**: `Waiting for Review`
- **State**: `Waiting for Review`
  - **Action**: `Review` (by `Purchase Manager`)
  - **Next State**: `Waiting for Approval`
- **State**: `Waiting for Approval`
  - **Action**: `Approve` (by `Head of Department`)
  - **Next State**: `Approved`

## Key Configuration Details

> [!TIP]
> You can disable automatic email alerts for workflow actions using the "Send Email Alert" checkbox.

- **States Table**:
  - `State`: The name of the workflow state (e.g., `Waiting for Review`).
  - `Doc Status`: The document's status code (0 for Draft, 1 for Submitted, 2 for Cancelled). For the final `Approved` state, setting this to `1` ensures the document is submitted and becomes read-only.
  - `Allow Edit`: Specify the **Role** that can modify the document when it is in this state.

- **Transition Rules Table**:
  - `State`: The current state of the document.
  - `Action`: The action a user performs (e.g., `Review`).
  - `Next State`: The state the document moves to after the action is completed.
  - `Allowed`: The **Role** that is permitted to perform this action.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> When you save a workflow for a doctype, ERPNext automatically adds a custom field named `workflow_state` to that doctype to track its progress. Once a document reaches a state with `Doc Status` set to `1` (Submitted), it cannot be edited further.

Or you can go into settings if you have the access to this. So you will go into settings and in settings down here you can see workflow.

So there are three type of things that you have to remember. One is the workflow state and one is the workflow action. Action is the type of action which a user is going to take to complete the workflow and state is the state of the workflow at that on which state or on which stage the current document is. So I'll explain you with the help of example. You can click on workflow or we'll open the workflow list and you will see all the existing workflows available. I will just click on add a workflow.

First action will be submit for review. If you see this action, action will be submit for review. I submit this review now it will be changing the state to waiting for review. Person will go back and check everything is fine and click on action and approve.

Now you can see the document has been approved. Approved state has been changed and now document is also submitted.
